So the function is simply returning the length of the input string.

[DESCRIPTION]: The function f(x) takes a string input and returns its length — the number of characters in the string, counting every character (including spaces, tabs, newlines, digits, punctuation, and unicode codepoints) exactly as-is without any trimming or normalization. For multiple arguments, it appears to print the length of each argument on its own line (or the harness calls it per-argument). Empty string returns 0.

[CODE]:

def f(x):
    return len(x)
